notes: The booklet really builds FIVE separate mini robots (model 1 steps 1-34, model 2 steps 35-69, model 3 steps 70-84, model 4 steps 85-118, model 5 steps 119-147). The cover shows them standing side by side but no step ever joins one robot to another, so the five separate groups are correct and are kept; inside each model every sub-assembly is connected by stud contact or by pin/axle/clip/hinge joins.

Each model uses its own region of the shared grid so models never overlap: model 1 at x 0-23, model 2 at x 100-154, model 3 at x 200-212, model 4 at x 299-353, model 5 at x 400-413. Sub-assemblies of one model are spaced apart in x (e.g. +10, +20, +30).
Step numbers run through the whole booklet counting sub-assemblies and part-less steps (rotations, folding, attaching sub-assemblies).

Piece ids were assigned by matching shape, colour and count of the booklet parts list to the piece list. The four lever bases (298c02) are the antennas (black p97,p98 on robot 1; white p99,p100 on robot 2).

Technic pieces (beams, pins, axles, connectors, wheels, hinge parts) have no stud-grid position (null) and rests_on []; their connections are in other_joins. Copies of identical pieces added in one step are assigned arbitrarily.

Some grid positions are approximate because isometric drawings hide cells; stacked heights assume bricks 3 plates and plates/tiles/brackets 1 plate. Smooth tiles are never rested upon. Sub-assemblies that are flipped or folded (robot 1 arm, robot 2 chassis and lid, rover chain) are recorded in final orientation; positions of such pieces may not match their sub-assembly orientation exactly.

notes: The booklet builds five separate mini robots (Robot, Dog? no: Mini Robot 1 = bipedal inventor, 2 = round-bellied robot, 3 = dog, 4 = rover with swap-able arm/binoculars, 5 = claw-arm rover). Each model is placed in its own local frame (x,y,layer start at 0 per sub-assembly); sub-assemblies of one model sit at different x offsets (e.g. +10, +20, +30).

Step numbers run through the whole booklet: model 1 = steps 1-34, model 2 = 35-69, model 3 = 70-84, model 4 = 85-118, model 5 = 119-147. Steps that add no parts (rotations, folding, attaching sub-assemblies) still count as steps.
Piece ids were assigned to booklet parts by matching shape/colour/count to the piece list. The four lever bases (298c02) are the antennas (black p97,p98 on robot 1; white p99,p100 on robot 2).

Technic pieces (beams, pins, axles, connectors, wheels, hinge parts) have no stud-grid position (null) and rests_on []; their connections are in other_joins. Where several identical copies are added in one step, the copy-to-position assignment is arbitrary.
Several grid positions are approximate because the isometric drawings do not show every stud cell clearly; rests_on follows the pieces that visibly sit under each piece.

Smooth tiles are only placed on studded pieces and nothing rests on them. Sub-assemblies that are folded/flipped (robot 1 arm, robot 2 chassis and lid, rover chains) are recorded in their final orientation.
